title: John Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 11.

questions.question: In John 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A certain man was sick named Lazarus
Thomas said, Let us also go, that we may die with him
Jesus said, This sickness is not unto death
questions.correctAnswer: A certain man was sick named Lazarus
questions.explanation: John 11:1 introduces the man named Lazarus who was sick, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who was Lazarus' sister who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair?
questions.correctAnswer: Mary
questions.explanation: John 11:2 states that Mary anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair.

questions.question: What did Lazarus' sisters say to Jesus about Lazarus' condition?
options: Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick
Please come quickly to heal Lazarus
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick
questions.explanation: John 11:3 records that Lazarus' sisters sent a message saying, 'Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.'

questions.question: What did Jesus say about Lazarus' sickness?
options: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God
Lazarus will never be well again
questions.correctAnswer: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God
questions.explanation: John 11:4 states that Jesus said the sickness is not unto death but for God's glory.

questions.question: Whom did Jesus love according to John 11?
questions.correctAnswer: Martha, her sister, and Lazarus
questions.explanation: John 11:5 says that Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.

questions.question: How long did Jesus stay in the same place after hearing Lazarus was sick?
questions.correctAnswer: Two days
questions.explanation: John 11:6 states that Jesus abode two days still where he was after hearing Lazarus was sick.

questions.question: Where did Jesus decide to go after two days?
questions.correctAnswer: Judaea
questions.explanation: John 11:7 records Jesus saying to his disciples, 'Let us go into Judaea again.'

questions.question: What concern did Jesus' disciples express about going to Judaea?
options: The Jews sought to stone Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews sought to stone Jesus
questions.explanation: John 11:8 shows the disciples saying, 'The Jews of late sought to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?'

questions.question: What did Jesus say about walking in the day?
options: If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not
Walking in the day is dangerous
Walking in the day causes blindness
People should avoid walking in the day
questions.correctAnswer: If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not
questions.explanation: John 11:9 states that Jesus said if any man walks in the day, he stumbleth not because he sees the light.

questions.question: What did Jesus say Lazarus was doing when he mentioned sleep?
questions.correctAnswer: Our friend Lazarus sleepeth
questions.explanation: John 11:11 records Jesus saying, 'Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.'

questions.question: How did Jesus clarify what he meant about Lazarus' sleep?
questions.correctAnswer: Lazarus is dead
questions.explanation: John 11:14 shows Jesus plainly telling them, 'Lazarus is dead.'

questions.question: True or False: Lazarus was the brother of Mary and Martha.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: John 11:1 and 11:2 confirm Lazarus was the brother of Mary and Martha.

questions.question: True or False: Thomas suggested they go with Jesus so that they might die with Lazarus.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: John 11:16 records Thomas saying, 'Let us also go, that we may die with him.'

questions.question: True or False: The text says Jesus immediately went to Lazarus as soon as he heard he was sick.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 11:6 states Jesus stayed two days longer where he was before going to Lazarus.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Lazarus was buried for four days before Jesus arrived.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 11:17 says Lazarus had lain in the grave four days; it does not specify he was buried for four days before Jesus arrived.

medium.title: John Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Martha say to Jesus when she first meets Him regarding her brother Lazarus?
options: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
Lord, why hast thou forsaken us?
Lord, come and heal him now.
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
questions.explanation: John 11:21 records Martha saying to Jesus, 'Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.'

questions.question: What does John 11:25 promise will happen if someone believes in Jesus, as commanded in John 11:26?
options: He that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.
He shall be rich and prosperous.
He shall be free from all sickness.
questions.correctAnswer: He that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.
questions.explanation: John 11:25 states, 'I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live,' which follows John 11:26’s command to believe in Jesus.

questions.question: How does Jesus describe Himself to Martha concerning life and resurrection?
options: I am the resurrection, and the life.
I am the bread of life.
I am the light of the world.
questions.correctAnswer: I am the resurrection, and the life.
questions.explanation: Jesus declares in John 11:25, 'I am the resurrection, and the life,' identifying Himself as the source of eternal life and resurrection.

questions.question: Connecting John 11:32 and John 11:35, what is the significance of Jesus weeping after seeing Mary and the Jews weeping?
options: It shows Jesus’ deep compassion and love for Lazarus and his family.
It reveals Jesus’ sorrow because He failed to heal Lazarus.
It indicates Jesus’ confusion about death.
It shows Jesus’ anger toward death.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Jesus’ deep compassion and love for Lazarus and his family.
questions.explanation: John 11:32-35 shows Jesus weeping after seeing Mary and the Jews weeping, demonstrating His compassion and love for those mourning Lazarus.

questions.question: What question does Jesus ask Martha to challenge her faith in John 11:26?
questions.correctAnswer: Believest thou this?
questions.explanation: In John 11:26, Jesus asks Martha, 'Believest thou this?' to challenge her belief in His claim of being life and resurrection.

questions.question: According to John 11:27, what does Martha confess about Jesus?
options: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.
You are the son of Joseph.
questions.correctAnswer: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.
questions.explanation: John 11:27 records Martha’s confession of faith, recognizing Jesus as the Christ and Son of God.

questions.question: What does Martha do immediately after her confession in John 11:28?
options: She went and called Mary her sister secretly.
She went to the town to tell others.
questions.correctAnswer: She went and called Mary her sister secretly.
questions.explanation: John 11:28 says Martha went to call Mary secretly after confessing her belief to Jesus.

questions.question: How do the Jews interpret Jesus’ weeping in John 11:36?
questions.correctAnswer: Behold how he loved him!
questions.explanation: John 11:36 records the Jews’ reaction to Jesus weeping as evidence of His love for Lazarus.

questions.question: Why do some Jews question Jesus’ power after Lazarus’ death according to John 11:37?
options: Could not this man, which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died?
Why does he not heal everyone?
Why does he not raise all the dead?
questions.correctAnswer: Could not this man, which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died?
questions.explanation: John 11:37 shows some Jews doubting Jesus’ power to prevent Lazarus’ death despite His miracles.

questions.question: What does Jesus do when He arrives at the grave in John 11:38?
options: He groans in himself and comes to the grave.
He commands the stone to be removed.
questions.correctAnswer: He groans in himself and comes to the grave.
questions.explanation: John 11:38 states Jesus groaned in Himself as He approached the grave, showing His deep emotion.

questions.question: What does John 11:20 reveal about Mary’s actions when she hears Jesus is coming?
options: Mary sat still in the house.
Mary went to the grave to weep.
questions.correctAnswer: Mary sat still in the house.
questions.explanation: John 11:20 says Mary stayed in the house when she heard Jesus was coming, unlike Martha who went out.

questions.question: What reason does Jesus give in John 11:4 for Lazarus’ sickness?
options: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God.
It is a punishment for sin.
It is to test the faith of his family.
questions.correctAnswer: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God.
questions.explanation: In John 11:4, Jesus explains Lazarus’ sickness is intended to glorify God through the Son of God.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus wept because He was sorrowful that Lazarus had died.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: John 11:33-35 shows Jesus was troubled and wept upon seeing the sorrow of Mary and the Jews, demonstrating His empathy and sorrow.

questions.question: True or False: Martha tells Jesus to leave because she does not believe He can raise Lazarus.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 11:21-24 shows Martha expressing faith that Lazarus will rise again and does not tell Jesus to leave.

questions.question: True or False: After hearing that Jesus had come, Mary delayed before going to meet Him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 11:29 says Mary 'arose quickly' and went to Jesus immediately after hearing He was calling.

hard.title: John Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 11.

questions.question: What reason does Martha give for hesitating to remove the stone from Lazarus' tomb?
options: He hath been dead four days and by this time he stinketh
The stone is too heavy to move
The tomb is sealed by the Romans
questions.correctAnswer: He hath been dead four days and by this time he stinketh
questions.explanation: Martha says this in John 11:39, expressing concern about the odor because Lazarus had been dead for four days.

questions.question: What does Jesus say will be seen if Martha believes?
questions.correctAnswer: The glory of God
questions.explanation: Jesus tells Martha in John 11:40 that if she believes, she will see the glory of God.

questions.question: What does Jesus do immediately after the stone is taken away from Lazarus' tomb?
options: He lifts up his eyes and thanks the Father
He lays hands on the tomb
He calls the disciples to pray
questions.correctAnswer: He lifts up his eyes and thanks the Father
questions.explanation: John 11:41 describes Jesus lifting up his eyes and thanking the Father after the stone was removed.

questions.question: Why does Jesus say he spoke aloud when praying before raising Lazarus?
options: So that the people standing by would believe that the Father sent him
To show his authority over death
questions.correctAnswer: So that the people standing by would believe that the Father sent him
questions.explanation: Jesus explains in John 11:42 that he prayed aloud so the crowd might believe that God sent him.

questions.question: What command does Jesus give to Lazarus after he comes out of the tomb?
options: Loose him, and let him go
questions.correctAnswer: Loose him, and let him go
questions.explanation: John 11:44 records Jesus instructing those present to unbind Lazarus and let him go after his resurrection.

questions.question: What was the reaction of many Jews who had come to Mary and saw what Jesus did?
options: They reported him to the Romans
questions.correctAnswer: They believed on him
questions.explanation: John 11:45 says that many of the Jews who came to Mary believed in Jesus after witnessing the miracle.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'epistamai' in John 11:49 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Know or understand
questions.explanation: In John 11:49, the Greek word 'epistamai' means 'know' or 'understand,' as Caiaphas says, 'Ye know nothing at all.'

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in John 11:25-26 where Jesus says, 'I am the resurrection, and the life'?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Jesus uses metaphorical language in John 11:25-26 identifying himself as 'the resurrection and the life,' symbolizing spiritual truth.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy is fulfilled by Caiaphas' statement in John 11:51 about one man dying for the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 53:10
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:10 foretells the suffering servant who dies for the people, which Caiaphas prophetically references in John 11:51.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Jesus raising Lazarus by emphasizing belief in Jesus' power over death?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 6:8-11
questions.explanation: Romans 6:8-11 discusses being united with Christ in his resurrection from the dead, echoing the theme of Jesus' power over death seen in John 11.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus' raising of Lazarus as described in John 11:38?
options: Jesus groaning in himself and coming to the grave
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus groaning in himself and coming to the grave
questions.explanation: John 11:38 says Jesus groaned again in himself and came to the grave just before instructing to remove the stone in verse 39.

questions.question: What is the significance of Lazarus being dead for four days before Jesus arrives, considering Jewish burial customs?
options: It confirms the death was certain and the soul had departed
It was the maximum time allowed for mourning
It symbolized impurity that lasts seven days
It matched the period for Passover preparation
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms the death was certain and the soul had departed
questions.explanation: Jewish belief held that the soul hovered near the body for three days; four days meant death was beyond doubt, as implied in John 11:39.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Lazarus' resurrection function as a typology for Jesus' own resurrection in John 11?
options: It prefigures Jesus’ victory over death and promise of eternal life
It symbolizes the end of the Mosaic law
It represents the division between Pharisees and Sadducees
It predicts the destruction of the Temple
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Jesus’ victory over death and promise of eternal life
questions.explanation: Lazarus’ resurrection in John 11 foreshadows Jesus’ own resurrection, showing his power over death and the gift of eternal life.

questions.question: What rhetorical purpose does Jesus' question in John 11:40 serve in the context of the narrative?
options: It challenges Martha’s doubt and calls for faith to witness God’s glory
It rebukes the Jewish leaders for their unbelief
It requests permission to perform the miracle
questions.correctAnswer: It challenges Martha’s doubt and calls for faith to witness God’s glory
questions.explanation: In John 11:40, Jesus confronts Martha’s doubt by emphasizing belief as the key to seeing God’s glory through the miracle.

questions.question: True or False: According to John 11:54, Jesus ceased to walk openly among the Jews after the council decided to put him to death.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: John 11:54 states that Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews after the plot to kill him began.

theological.title: John Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 11:4 teach about the purpose of suffering and death in relation to God's glory?
options: Suffering is meaningless and without purpose
Sickness and death are opportunities for the Son of God to be glorified
God causes suffering as punishment only
Sickness always leads to eternal death
questions.correctAnswer: Sickness and death are opportunities for the Son of God to be glorified
questions.explanation: John 11:4 states that the sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God might be glorified by it, teaching that suffering can serve God's redemptive purpose.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' identity is revealed in John 11:25?
options: Jesus is a prophet who foretells resurrection
Jesus identifies Himself as the resurrection and the life, indicating His divine authority over death
Jesus is only a teacher of moral truths
Jesus is an angel sent to comfort believers
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus identifies Himself as the resurrection and the life, indicating His divine authority over death
questions.explanation: John 11:25 records Jesus saying, 'I am the resurrection, and the life,' affirming His divine role as conqueror of death and source of eternal life.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning faith and belief is emphasized in John 11:26?
options: Only works save a person, not belief
Belief in Jesus leads to eternal life and conquers spiritual death
Faith is irrelevant to eternal life
questions.correctAnswer: Belief in Jesus leads to eternal life and conquers spiritual death
questions.explanation: John 11:26 teaches that whoever lives and believes in Jesus shall never die, emphasizing faith as the means to eternal life beyond physical death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 11:35 specifically demonstrate through Jesus' reaction to Lazarus' death?
questions.correctAnswer: Compassion
questions.explanation: John 11:35 states 'Jesus wept,' showing His deep compassion and empathy for human sorrow.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by Jesus’ confident prayer in John 11:42 before raising Lazarus?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreknowledge
questions.explanation: In John 11:42, Jesus expresses certainty that the Father always hears Him, demonstrating His foreknowledge and intimate relationship with God.

questions.question: How does the raising of Lazarus in John 11 prepare for the ultimate resurrection and eternal life promised in the New Testament?
options: It is an isolated miracle unrelated to Christian hope
It serves as a sign pointing forward to Christ’s own resurrection and the future resurrection of believers
It disproves the doctrine of resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as a sign pointing forward to Christ’s own resurrection and the future resurrection of believers
questions.explanation: John 11’s resurrection of Lazarus prefigures Christ’s victory over death and the promise of resurrection for all who believe, linking to 1 Corinthians 15.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is made by John 11:50–51 concerning the death of Jesus?
options: Jesus’ death was accidental with no divine plan
Jesus’ death was foretold by Caiaphas as necessary to prevent the nation’s destruction and to gather scattered believers
Jesus’ death ended the Jewish covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ death was foretold by Caiaphas as necessary to prevent the nation’s destruction and to gather scattered believers
questions.explanation: John 11:50–51 reveals Caiaphas prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation and gather God's children, showing divine providence in the passion.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 11:4 and John 11:25 teach about the relationship between Jesus’ glory and eternal life?
options: Jesus’ glory is unrelated to eternal life
Jesus’ glorification through suffering reveals His authority as the source of resurrection and life
Eternal life is a human achievement
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ glorification through suffering reveals His authority as the source of resurrection and life
questions.explanation: John 11:4 shows suffering glorifies the Son of God; John 11:25 identifies Jesus as resurrection and life, linking His glorification with granting eternal life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 11:26 and John 11:27 teach concerning the nature of faith in Christ?
options: True faith recognizes Jesus as the Christ and leads to eternal life that overcomes death
questions.correctAnswer: True faith recognizes Jesus as the Christ and leads to eternal life that overcomes death
questions.explanation: John 11:26 promises eternal life to believers; 11:27 affirms belief in Jesus as the Christ, emphasizing faith’s saving nature.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 11:35 and John 11:36 reveal about Jesus' nature in relation to human emotion and divine love?
options: Jesus is indifferent to human suffering
Jesus displays true human emotion, demonstrating divine love and empathy
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus displays true human emotion, demonstrating divine love and empathy
questions.explanation: John 11:35 shows Jesus wept; 11:36 confirms His love for Lazarus, illustrating His genuine humanity and divine compassion.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jesus’ statement in John 11:25–26 is metaphorical and not a promise of literal resurrection. What does John 11:25–26 actually teach?
options: Jesus speaks symbolically about spiritual rebirth only
Jesus claims to have authority over physical death and promises actual resurrection to eternal life
Jesus’ words are ambiguous and open to interpretation
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus claims to have authority over physical death and promises actual resurrection to eternal life
questions.explanation: John 11:25–26 explicitly connects belief in Jesus with life after physical death, affirming literal resurrection and eternal life.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine timing and human faith is taught in John 11:6?
options: Jesus’ delay in going to Lazarus emphasizes that God’s timing is sovereign and faith must persist amid waiting
Jesus was unaware of Lazarus’ condition
Delay shows a lack of care
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ delay in going to Lazarus emphasizes that God’s timing is sovereign and faith must persist amid waiting
questions.explanation: John 11:6 shows Jesus stayed two days before going, teaching that God’s timing serves a greater purpose and believers must trust amid delays.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by Jesus’ intentional use of the term 'sleep' for death in John 11:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over death
questions.explanation: John 11:11 uses 'sleep' to indicate Jesus’ power to 'awake' Lazarus, showing His sovereign control over death itself.

questions.question: How does the narrative arc of John 11:53–54 prepare for the passion and resurrection narratives later in the Gospel?
options: It shows Jesus’ rejection and the plotting of His death, setting the stage for the passion
It ends the story of Jesus’ ministry
It focuses only on Jewish political issues
It predicts Jesus’ triumph without suffering
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Jesus’ rejection and the plotting of His death, setting the stage for the passion
questions.explanation: John 11:53–54 records the council’s plan to kill Jesus and His consequent withdrawal, foreshadowing the passion narrative.

questions.question: What theological significance does John 11:40 reveal about the relationship between faith and witnessing God's glory?
options: Faith is unnecessary to see God's glory
Belief is a prerequisite to experiencing God's glory revealed in Jesus' miracles
God’s glory is hidden regardless of faith
Glory is only for the righteous by birth
questions.correctAnswer: Belief is a prerequisite to experiencing God's glory revealed in Jesus' miracles
questions.explanation: Jesus tells Martha in John 11:40 that if she believes, she will see the glory of God, illustrating faith as necessary to perceive divine revelation.
